profile.headline: Data SWE @ Google Maps - Walking/Biking/Transit Advocate
profile.summary:
I work on things that 1) get people out of cars and 2) get cars out of cities.

If you can figure out what city is in my header photo, I will accept your connection request and/or buy you a burrito 🌯

Otherwise, I only add people I know. If you are interested in chatting with me about Google, send me a connection request and include a message, and I will respond!

I like data, geography, math, ML, cities, and alternative transportation. I value working with ethical, empathetic, smart, communicative, kind people.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I work on cool ways to aggregate and use user transportation data in Google Maps.

The team I'm on creates the semantic location history data you see in Timeline in Google Maps. My job is to transform & aggregate that data - especially data about public transit, bicycling, and walking - and create value for Maps users. Currently, I'm working on integrating Timeline data into the recently-launched Ask Maps, an LLM discovery and planning tool in Maps.

In April 2026, I helped launch the Cycling Trip Percentage layer in Google Earth. This data layer shows the bicycling modal share all around the world, and is derived from the daily activity of hundreds of millions of Maps users who have opted into Timeline. I owned, designed, and built the data aggregation, anonymization (through Differential Privacy), and data quality pieces of this project. This launch was featured in the Google Earth blog post below.

When the COVID pandemic hit, I helped build a prototype model to predict crowdedness on transit vehicles. After that model was launched, I took ownership of the project and rebuilt it into a robust, fully machine-learned model. The launch of that model was featured in the Google Keyword blog post below.

I've worked on some other projects related to measuring real-world transportation across the world and using it to improve Google Maps, such as improving the in-station walking time estimates that Maps shows users in transit directions.
positions.insights: Skills: Data Engineering · Data Quality · Distributed Data Processing · Transportation Data · Big Data Analytics

positions.title: Data Scientist
positions.description:
Zenabi was a young data science and software consulting company.  I supported three different projects as a data scientist.

One is for a global nonprofit org, where I maintained a model that predicted the likelihood that prospective members will join.  I was responsible for this model from end to end - from feature engineering to machine learning to deployment and delivery via API.  I also supported other team members on this project in efforts involving email marketing and website content recommendation engines. 

The second was for the NYC subway.  I prototyped a model that predicts delays on individual lines with minute-level precision.  I spearheaded the project and, with two coworkers, pitched our solution to a panel of MTA management and VCs.

The third was for a company that provides loans for small and medium-sized businesses. As the lead and only data scientist on the project, I provided expertise and analysis and began the process of moving their existing approval model from DataRobot to a custom, Zenabi-hosted solution.

positions.title: Data Engineer
positions.description: I implemented parts of an in-house user event tracking system for Lucidchart in both TypeScript and Scala.  I also built ETL pipelines using Python, Scala, and SQL to provide data for and support the efforts of the data scientists.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
As a member of the Diagram Automation team, I maintained Lucidchart's CSV import feature.  I also supported other diagram auto-creation and auto-layout features, such as AWS Import and ERD Import.

I worked on a scrum team in two-week sprints, participated in frequent code reviews, and wrote unit tests.  I wrote mostly TypeScript (including some Angular) and a little Scala.

positions.title: Strategy and Geospatial Analysis Intern
positions.description: I used Python to aggregate and clean geographic data about consumers, businesses, and competing branches.  I then used regression to isolate key metrics for predicting success of future branch locations.

positions.title: Student Leader and Curriculum Developer
positions.description:
I led the Student Advisory Council for ACME.  In this capacity, I led weekly student committee meetings where we planned social and career-building activities for the ACME students.

I also contributed to the ACME curriculum by writing and reviewing Python lessons for the ACME lab classes.

positions.title: Earth Science Research Intern
positions.description: As a participant in NASA's Student Airborne Research Program, I researched mathematical approaches to earth systems science.  In particular, my research focused on distinguishing different species of kelp in airborne and satellite imagery using algorithmic techniques.  My preliminary research was successful in accomplishing this, and I was awarded a NASA scholarship to attend the AGU annual meeting in San Francisco and present my research.

company.name: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: I worked on both the engineering and the analytics sides of the Growth team. On the engineering side, I designed and implemented a multi-armed bandit algorithm in the company's Scala code base.  On the analytics side, I analyzed the results of the bandit algorithm and wrote a blog post about it (see below).  I also cleaned, processed, and analyzed usage data from LucidChart using Python.

positions.title: Regional Manager/Translator
positions.description:
I traveled to Germany with the SolidPartners team and worked the booth at the 2016 Hannover Messe, the largest industrial trade fair in the world.  At the fair, I represented the company and its software products and translated between English and German as often as needed.  After the fair, I visited with company contacts throughout Germany, doing software demos with my coworker.

In addition, I coordinated and purchased intercontinental as well as European travel and accommodations for the team, and simply acted as the point man for all things German.

positions.title: Teacher's Assistant
positions.description: I assisted Dr. Brandon Campbell with Physics 220: Electricity and Magnetism.

positions.title: Construction Design Intern
positions.description: I pieced together several sets of data about the company's subcontractors from outdated databases and prepared the data for a new database.  I used lots of Excel, including VBA.  I also did other projects involving data manipulation and visualization in Excel.

volunteerExperiences.description:
🚶🚲 🚍 🏘️ 🌳

Sustainable Streets advocates for walking, biking, public transportation, housing, and urban greenery in Norwalk.

My job is to find like-minded people and enable them to make the change they want to make. Mostly this happens over lunch, which is the best way to do anything.

So far, we've accomplished the following:
- organized a successful effort to eliminate parking requirements in Norwalk's downtown zone - this included submitting a four-page written memo to the Planning & Zoning Commission and turning 10 people out to the public hearing
- turned 10-15 speakers out to public hearings on city & state projects to advocate for walking, biking, and transit infrastructure 
- built a social media following of 1000+
- held a weekly social all-abilities bike ride for two seasons (May-October)
- held several public social events, including three bus-oriented pub crawls

As chair, I led the following initiatives on the Commission:
- Filling commission vacancies with young & diverse candidates
- Completing the extensive Bicycle Friendly Community application and seeing Norwalk recognized with an Honorable Mention
- Conceiving, planning, and successfully executing the Calf Pasture Beach Open Street event two years running
- Conceiving and launching the Bicycle Valet Parking program
- Compiling and delivering a master bicycle parking wish list to TMP
- Sending Vanessa Valadares, Chief of Operations & Public Works, and myself to the Harvard seminar "The Walkable City", taught by Jeff Speck.
- Organizing a community screening of The Street Project, a documentary by a local CT filmmaker about the fight for safe streets

projects.title: Kelp Mapping with Machine Learning
projects.description:
In February 2017, I received a student research grant from BYU to continue the work I did at SARP the previous summer and publish my research.  Since then, I have worked with BYU Professors Ryan Jensen (Geography) and Tyler Jarvis (Mathematics) to bring my work up to the level it needs to be in order to publish.

Among other things, I have:
1) Automated my data mining process, giving me 100x the amount of training data
2) Applied several new machine learning models to the data, achieving an accuracy of 99.7%
3) Written a formal literature review

We are now working on the final write-up.  Our aim is to submit the paper to the Journal of Applied Remote Sensing by mid-December.

volunteerExperience.description:
🚶🚲 🚍 🏘️ 🌳

Sustainable Streets advocates for walking, biking, public transportation, housing, and urban greenery in Norwalk.

My job is to find like-minded people and enable them to make the change they want to make. Mostly this happens over lunch, which is the best way to do anything.

So far, we've accomplished the following:
- organized a successful effort to eliminate parking requirements in Norwalk's downtown zone - this included submitting a four-page written memo to the Planning & Zoning Commission and turning 10 people out to the public hearing
- turned 10-15 speakers out to public hearings on city & state projects to advocate for walking, biking, and transit infrastructure 
- built a social media following of 1000+
- held a weekly social all-abilities bike ride for two seasons (May-October)
- held several public social events, including three bus-oriented pub crawls

As chair, I led the following initiatives on the Commission:
- Filling commission vacancies with young & diverse candidates
- Completing the extensive Bicycle Friendly Community application and seeing Norwalk recognized with an Honorable Mention
- Conceiving, planning, and successfully executing the Calf Pasture Beach Open Street event two years running
- Conceiving and launching the Bicycle Valet Parking program
- Compiling and delivering a master bicycle parking wish list to TMP
- Sending Vanessa Valadares, Chief of Operations & Public Works, and myself to the Harvard seminar "The Walkable City", taught by Jeff Speck.
- Organizing a community screening of The Street Project, a documentary by a local CT filmmaker about the fight for safe streets
